Format Long-Format Repeated Measures Data for Because Analysis

Source: R/because_format_data.R
because_format_data.Rd

Converts data from long format (multiple rows per unit/group, such as repeated measurements per individual, site survey visits, or within-species replicates) to the named list format (unit-level vectors and replicate matrices) used by because for error-in-variables (variability = "reps"), detection/occupancy models, and structured covariance models.

Usage

because_format_data(
  data,
  id_col = "ID",
  structure = NULL,
  species_col = NULL,
  tree = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame in long format with one row per observation.

id_col

Name of the column containing unit identifiers (e.g., individual, site, or species IDs; default: "ID", falling back to "SP" if present).

structure

Optional covariance structure object (e.g., a spatial/pedigree matrix with row names, a because_structure object, or a phylogenetic tree). If provided, determines the ordering of units in the output.

species_col

Deprecated alias for id_col (retained for backward compatibility).

tree

Deprecated alias for structure (retained for backward compatibility).

Value

A named list where each element is either:

  • A named numeric vector (if a variable is constant within each unit or all units have 1 observation)

  • A numeric matrix with units in rows and replicates in columns (padded with NA)

Units are ordered to match the labels of structure (if provided) or sorted alphabetically.

Details

This function handles:

  • Different numbers of replicates per unit (creates a rectangular matrix with NA padding)

  • Automatic distinction between unit-constant covariates (returned as vectors) and replicate-varying measurements (returned as matrices)

  • Missing values (NA)

  • Automatic alignment with covariance structure labels (e.g., matrix row names or phylogenetic tree tip labels, if structure is provided)

When units have different numbers of replicates, the function creates a matrix with dimensions (number of units) x (maximum number of replicates). Units with fewer replicates are padded with NA values.

If a structure is provided:

  • Units present in the structure but missing from data receive all NA values (enabling Bayesian imputation).

  • Units present in data but absent from the structure are excluded with a warning.

If no structure is provided: All units in data are included, sorted alphabetically by their identifier.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Example 1: General repeated measures / Error-in-Variables (no structure)
data_long <- data.frame(
  ID   = c("ind1", "ind1", "ind1", "ind2", "ind2", "ind3"),
  Age  = c(3, 3, 3, 5, 5, 2),          # Constant within individual -> vector
  Mass = c(1.2, 1.3, 1.1, 2.1, 2.2, 1.8), # Varying -> matrix (3 x 3)
  Cort = c(0.5, 0.6, NA, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9)   # Varying -> matrix (3 x 3)
)
data_list <- because_format_data(data_long, id_col = "ID")

# Example 2: Aligning with a covariance matrix (e.g., spatial or pedigree)
prec_mat <- diag(3)
rownames(prec_mat) <- colnames(prec_mat) <- c("ind3", "ind1", "ind2")
data_aligned <- because_format_data(data_long, id_col = "ID", structure = prec_mat)
} # }
